newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PGGM doubtful high returns will continue.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PGGM doubtful high returns will continue.

text.p: Dutch health sector pension fund PGGM said on Tuesday it was not optimistic that its current high returns would continue.

PGGM, the second largest Dutch pension fund with assets under management of 65.9 billion guilders at December 31, earlier announced it had realised a return of 15.9 percent on its investments in 1996, up from 13.1 percent in 1995.

The result was mainly due to the high percentage of shares within its portfolio, which yielded a 26 percent return, compared to 8.4 percent from fixed interest investments and 10.1 percent from property.
Dick de Beus, chairman of PGGM's board of managing directors, said share markets had performed extremely well in 1995 and 1996 but he realised this could not continue forever.
"I'm not optimistic that it's possible to continue the high rates of return," he told Reuters after a news conference on the fund's 1996 results.
But he said it was too early to give a specific forecast for the likely return in 1997, adding that recent experience had shown the stock market could be very volatile.
"For us, developments in relation to the stockmarket are very important," de Beus said.
PGGM, second in size only to public-sector fund ABP among Dutch pension funds, has been lifting its exposure to equities in recent years in a bid to boost long term returns.
At the end of 1996, 47 percent of its funds were invested in shares, up from none in 1983 and eight percent in 1986.
The proportion of its portfolio held in fixed-interest investments has fallen to 41 percent from 77 percent since 1986.
De Beus said research had shown investments in equities would produce higher long term returns than other asset categories.
PGGM wants to hold between 50 and 60 percent of its portfolio in equities.
He said the current allocation to shares was 50 percent, adding that developments in sharemarkets would determine how it fluctuated within this band.
PGGM's real return, net of inflation, on its portfolio has averaged 3.3 percent over the long term, compared with 14-15 percent in 1996.
